deployments_detail.use: Future of Mining Challenge — Wheaton's US$1M corporate innovation program that solicits and funds AI-driven mining technologies. Program materials list eligible technology categories including Artificial Intelligence, and target areas such as 'AI-driven ore body characterization and predictive geology', 'sensor-based ore sorting and real-time grade control', and data-driven optimization of blasting/drilling/mine-to-mill workflows. (AI is deployed in the funded partner ventures, not by Wheaton itself.) [none named]
deployments_detail.value: US$1 million award per challenge cycle

deployments_detail.use: Future of Mining Challenge eligible-technology list explicitly enumerating Artificial Intelligence alongside Blockchain and Cloud Computing/IoT, in Wheaton's official launch press releases — confirming AI is a formally targeted innovation category the company backs financially. [none named]
Machine-learning ingestion pipeline parsing partner PDFs/data into standardized JSON to cut manual work and improve accuracy

Internal use of Company AI systems (including generative AI) for business purposes, governed by a dedicated Information Technology & Artificial Intelligence (ITAI) Committee that provides oversight, and by mandatory employee AI training/workshops. Wheaton's Board-level Technology Usage Policy (rev. August 2025) defines 'Company AI' as artificial intelligence systems, including generative AI, that are part of Company Systems, and sets rules for their responsible adoption and use. [none named]

Data-security controls governing employee use of external/third-party generative AI. Wheaton's Technology Usage Policy explicitly prohibits including Company Data in any input or submission to external generative AI systems (naming ChatGPT as the example), and reserves the right to monitor and disable AI usage — an information-security/risk control over generative-AI tooling in the corporate environment.
